persona.label: Busy, wants a callback
persona.description: At work and won't do it by text. Wants a call tomorrow after 5pm. Agent should book a callback, not push.
persona.behavior: You are a nurse on shift and can't text right now. Your first reply is "at work, can't do this now." If offered options, ask for someone to call you tomorrow after 5pm. Don't answer qualification questions by text; if pressed, say "I'd rather just talk tomorrow." Once a callback is confirmed, say thanks and stop replying.

transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
at work, can't do this now.
No problem, Sam. You can either answer 2-3 quick questions by text now, or pick a time for a loan officer to call you. Which works better?
can someone call me tomorrow after 5pm?
Your call is booked, Sam. A licensed loan officer from Harborline will call you at this number tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm.

events.name: schedule_callback

input.notes: Sam Ortiz submitted a refinance web inquiry. At work, no qualification details collected yet (goal, home value, balance, rate, credit, occupancy, timeline all still needed). Call at the number they texted from.

events.result: Callback booked. In one short message, confirm the time and say a licensed loan officer will call. Then close.

callback.notes: Sam Ortiz submitted a refinance web inquiry. At work, no qualification details collected yet (goal, home value, balance, rate, credit, occupancy, timeline all still needed). Call at the number they texted from.

objections.rationale: Agent offered exactly the two playbook options ("answer 2-3 quick questions by text now, or pick a time for a loan officer to call you"), then scheduled the callback when the borrower chose a time and ended politely without pushing for details.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm, and suited to text ("No problem, Sam."). The confirmation at [4] is clear and specific, giving the day and window. Turn [2] is slightly templated, and the close lacks a light sign-off such as "Talk soon" or a thanks, so it reads a bit abrupt.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower's busy signal at [1] was respected immediately, and at [4] they learned who will call ("A licensed loan officer from Harborline"), how ("at this number"), and when ("tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm"). It was a low-friction exchange with honest expectations.

annotations.note: The opener discloses AI identity ("an automated assistant"), gives the context of the inquiry, and offers STOP up front.
It acknowledges the borrower is busy and offers both playbook options concisely, without pressuring them to answer questions now.
The callback confirmation is specific ("tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm", "at this number") and avoids any rate or approval language.
The close ends without a brief thanks or a reminder that the borrower can reply to reschedule, which feels slightly abrupt.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant handling of a busy borrower that follows the playbook exactly and leaves the borrower with a concrete next step. The only room to improve is a warmer sign-off and an option to reschedule.
